# Expression Gallery catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:gallery` from js/fhir/expr-builder/gallery/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Ready-made calculation patterns offered by **📐 Choose from gallery** in the Expression Builder (35 patterns).
Pick a pattern, say which questionnaire item supplies each input, and the resulting FHIRPath is inserted as ordinary, editable text.

- Where an input offers several units, you choose the unit your item uses and the pattern converts it.
- Where a pattern lists an **answer code** input, it is prefilled with a default; change it if your answers use another code.
- Numeric and date patterns give **no result** until every input is answered, rather than guessing a value; yes/no checklist patterns count an unanswered box as No.
- Date patterns need full dates (year-month-day).
- These are reference calculations to save authoring effort, not medical advice. Check each formula against its source for your use case.

To add a pattern, see [the gallery README](../js/fhir/expr-builder/gallery/README.md).

| Pattern | What it computes | Inputs | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BMI (Body Mass Index)** | weight ÷ height² — pick the weight and height items, with optional unit conversion. | Weight item (Already in kg / Convert from lb)<br>Height item (Already in m / Convert from cm) | Quetelet index (weight kg ÷ height m²) |
| **BMI (imperial: lb, inches)** | weight(lb) × 703 ÷ height(in)² — the standard US imperial BMI formula. | Weight item (Already in lb / Convert from kg)<br>Height item (Already in inches / Convert from cm) | Imperial BMI formula (weight lb × 703 ÷ height in²) |
| **BMI Category (WHO)** | BMI mapped to its WHO weight category — pick the weight and height items, with optional unit conversion.<br>Result: Underweight · Normal weight · Overweight · Obese | Weight item (Already in kg / Convert from lb)<br>Height item (Already in m / Convert from cm) | WHO adult BMI classification |
| **Age from birthdate (whole years)** | Whole years since a birthdate item — correctly handles a birthday not yet reached this year. | Birthdate item | Calendar-year difference with birthday adjustment |
| **Unit conversion** | Convert a single numeric item between common clinical units. | Item to convert (lb → kg / kg → lb / cm → m / m → cm / °F → °C / °C → °F) | Standard unit conversion factors |
| **GAD-7 total + severity** | Sums the 7 GAD-7 items (each scored 0–3) and maps the total to its anxiety severity band.<br>Result: Minimal anxiety · Mild anxiety · Moderate anxiety · Severe anxiety | Q1 — feeling nervous, anxious, on edge<br>Q2 — unable to stop/control worrying<br>Q3 — worrying too much<br>Q4 — trouble relaxing<br>Q5 — restless<br>Q6 — easily annoyed/irritable<br>Q7 — feeling afraid something awful might happen | Spitzer et al. 2006, Arch Intern Med 166:1092 |
| **PHQ-9 total + severity** | Sums the 9 PHQ-9 items (each scored 0–3) and maps the total to its depression severity band.<br>Result: Minimal depression · Mild depression · Moderate depression · Moderately severe depression · Severe depression | Q1 — little interest or pleasure<br>Q2 — feeling down, depressed, hopeless<br>Q3 — sleep trouble<br>Q4 — tired / little energy<br>Q5 — poor appetite or overeating<br>Q6 — feeling bad about yourself<br>Q7 — trouble concentrating<br>Q8 — moving/speaking slowly, or restless<br>Q9 — thoughts of self-harm | Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2001, J Gen Intern Med 16:606 |
| **CHA₂DS₂-VASc stroke risk score** | Stroke risk score for atrial fibrillation — pick the yes/no item for each criterion (max 9 points). | Congestive heart failure / LV dysfunction (+1)<br>Hypertension (+1)<br>Age ≥75 (+2)<br>Diabetes mellitus (+1)<br>Prior stroke/TIA/thromboembolism (+2)<br>Vascular disease (+1)<br>Age 65–74 (+1)<br>Sex category female (+1) | Lip et al. 2010, Chest 137:263 |
| **Sum of items** | Add as many numeric items as you need — their values (with optional unit conversion) are added together. | Item to include (add as many rows as needed) (As-is / lb → kg / kg → lb / cm → m / m → cm / °F → °C / °C → °F) | Plain sum of the picked items |
| **Charlson Comorbidity Index** | Add one row per comorbidity the patient has — each contributes its fixed weight (1–6), plus an automatic age-based bonus. | Comorbidity present (add as many rows as needed) (Myocardial infarction (+1) / Congestive heart failure (+1) / Peripheral vascular disease (+1) / Cerebrovascular disease (+1) / Dementia (+1) / Chronic pulmonary disease (+1) / Rheumatologic disease (+1) / Peptic ulcer disease (+1) / Liver disease — mild (+1) / Diabetes — controlled (+1) / Hemiplegia or paraplegia (+2) / Renal disease (+2) / Diabetes — uncontrolled (end-organ damage) (+2) / Malignancy — localized (+2) / Leukemia (+2) / Lymphoma (+2) / Liver disease — moderate/severe (+3) / Malignancy — metastatic (+6) / AIDS (+6))<br>Age (years) | Charlson et al. 1987, J Chronic Dis 40:373 (with the Charlson/Deyo age adjustment) |
| **Count of Yes answers** | How many of the picked yes/no items are answered Yes — add one row per item. | Yes/no item (add as many rows as needed) | Plain count of the picked items answered Yes |
| **Percent change** | (new − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100, rounded to 1 decimal — e.g. weight change since the first visit. | Baseline value item<br>New value item | Standard relative change: (new − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100 |
| **PHQ-2 screen** | Sums the 2 PHQ-2 items (each scored 0–3); a total of 3 or more is a positive depression screen.<br>Result: Negative screen · Positive screen | Q1 — little interest or pleasure<br>Q2 — feeling down, depressed, hopeless | Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2003, Med Care 41:1284 |
| **Glasgow Coma Scale** | Adds the eye (1–4), verbal (1–5) and motor (1–6) responses and maps the total (3–15) to its severity band.<br>Result: Severe (GCS 3–8) · Moderate (GCS 9–12) · Mild (GCS 13–15) | Eye response (1–4)<br>Verbal response (1–5)<br>Motor response (1–6) | Teasdale & Jennett 1974, Lancet 2:81 |
| **Apgar score** | Sums the 5 Apgar criteria (each scored 0–2) and maps the total (0–10) to its band.<br>Result: Low (0–3) · Moderately abnormal (4–6) · Reassuring (7–10) | Appearance — skin colour (0–2)<br>Pulse — heart rate (0–2)<br>Grimace — reflex irritability (0–2)<br>Activity — muscle tone (0–2)<br>Respiration — breathing effort (0–2) | Apgar 1953; AAP/ACOG score bands |
| **qSOFA sepsis screen** | Counts the 3 qSOFA criteria that are present; 2 or more means high risk of poor outcome.<br>Result: Lower risk · High risk | Respiratory rate ≥22/min<br>Altered mentation<br>Systolic BP ≤100 mmHg | Singer et al. 2016 (Sepsis-3), JAMA 315:801 |
| **Body surface area (Mosteller)** | √(height cm × weight kg ÷ 3600), in m² — pick the height and weight items, with optional unit conversion. | Height item (Already in cm / Convert from inches / Convert from m)<br>Weight item (Already in kg / Convert from lb) | Mosteller 1987, N Engl J Med 317:1098 |
| **Mean arterial pressure** | (systolic + 2 × diastolic) ÷ 3 in mmHg, rounded to 1 decimal. | Systolic BP item<br>Diastolic BP item | Standard estimate: (systolic + 2 × diastolic) ÷ 3 |
| **Serum anion gap** | Na − (Cl + HCO₃), all in mEq/L — pick the three lab items. | Sodium item<br>Chloride item<br>Bicarbonate item | Standard potassium-free form: Na − (Cl + HCO₃) |
| **eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021)** | Estimated GFR in mL/min/1.73 m² from creatinine, age and sex — set the answer code that means female if your sex item does not use “female”. | Serum creatinine item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from µmol/L)<br>Age in years item<br>Sex item (single choice)<br>Answer code for Female (default `female`) | Inker et al. 2021, N Engl J Med 385:1737 (race-free CKD-EPI) |
| **Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft–Gault)** | (140 − age) × weight ÷ (72 × creatinine), × 0.85 if female, in mL/min — set the answer code that means female if your sex item does not use “female”. | Age in years item<br>Weight item (Already in kg / Convert from lb)<br>Serum creatinine item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from µmol/L)<br>Sex item (single choice)<br>Answer code for Female (default `female`) | Cockcroft & Gault 1976, Nephron 16:31 |
| **Expected delivery date (LMP + 280 days)** | Last menstrual period + 280 days (40 weeks), assuming a regular 28-day cycle. | Last menstrual period item | Naegele's rule, 280-day form (regular 28-day cycle) |
| **Date plus interval** | A date item plus a fixed interval — e.g. a follow-up or next-due date. | Start date item (+ 1 week / + 2 weeks / + 4 weeks / + 1 month / + 3 months / + 6 months / + 1 year) | FHIRPath calendar arithmetic |
| **Age at a date (whole years)** | Whole years between a birthdate and another date item — e.g. age at the visit or at diagnosis. | Birthdate item<br>Date to measure age at | Calendar-year difference with birthday adjustment |
| **Age in months at a date** | Whole months between a birthdate and another date item — for infant and paediatric questionnaires. | Birthdate item<br>Date to measure age at | Calendar-month difference with day-of-month adjustment |
| **Corrected calcium (albumin)** | Total calcium adjusted for low albumin, in mg/dL: Ca + 0.8 × (4.0 − albumin). | Total calcium item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from mmol/L)<br>Albumin item (Already in g/dL / Convert from g/L) | Payne et al. 1973, BMJ 4:643 |
| **LDL cholesterol (Friedewald)** | Total − HDL − triglycerides ÷ 5, in mg/dL; no result when triglycerides are 400 mg/dL or more. | Total cholesterol item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from mmol/L)<br>HDL cholesterol item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from mmol/L)<br>Triglycerides item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from mmol/L) | Friedewald et al. 1972, Clin Chem 18:499 |
| **HOMA-IR (insulin resistance)** | Fasting glucose × fasting insulin ÷ 405 (glucose in mg/dL, insulin in µU/mL), rounded to 2 decimals. | Fasting glucose item (Already in mg/dL / Convert from mmol/L)<br>Fasting insulin item (µU/mL) | Matthews et al. 1985, Diabetologia 28:412 |
| **FIB-4 liver fibrosis index** | Age × AST ÷ (platelets × √ALT), mapped to low / indeterminate / high risk of advanced fibrosis (cut-offs 1.3 and 2.67).<br>Result: Low risk (< 1.3) · Indeterminate (1.3–2.67) · High risk (> 2.67) | Age in years item<br>AST item (U/L)<br>ALT item (U/L)<br>Platelets item (×10⁹/L) | Shah et al. 2009, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 7:1104 (cut-offs 1.3 / 2.67) |
| **QTc (Bazett)** | QT interval corrected for heart rate: QT ÷ √RR, in ms — over-corrects at fast heart rates. | QT interval item (ms)<br>Heart rate item (bpm) | Bazett 1920 |
| **QTc (Fridericia)** | QT interval corrected for heart rate: QT ÷ RR¹ᐟ³, in ms — steadier than Bazett at fast or slow rates. | QT interval item (ms)<br>Heart rate item (bpm) | Fridericia 1920 |
| **Ideal body weight (Devine)** | Male 50 kg / female 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 feet — set the answer code that means female if your sex item does not use “female”. | Height item (Already in inches / Convert from cm)<br>Sex item (single choice)<br>Answer code for Female (default `female`) | Devine 1974, Drug Intell Clin Pharm 8:650 |
| **Waist-to-hip ratio** | Waist circumference ÷ hip circumference (same unit), rounded to 2 decimals. | Waist circumference item<br>Hip circumference item | WHO Expert Consultation 2008, Waist circumference and waist–hip ratio (Geneva) |
| **Days between two dates** | Whole days from a start date item to an end date item — e.g. length of stay. Negative if the end is before the start. | Start date item<br>End date item | Calendar day count (Gregorian calendar, leap years included) |
| **Gestational age (completed weeks)** | Completed weeks from the last menstrual period to a visit date item; no result if the visit is before the LMP. | Last menstrual period item<br>Visit date item | Standard LMP dating (completed weeks since the first day of the last period) |
